messages:
sanjay: FYI seeing a ~40% throughput drop on small-gpu-pool-3 starting ~12:36 UTC. Multiple worker restarts and a handful of GPU OOMs. Posting quick logs + perf snapshot. ping @ryan @kate

ryan: On it. Any recent kernel-selector changes rolled to that pool?

kate: I rolled kernel-selector v2.3 (int8-preferring) as a canary to small pools at 11:58 UTC. It biases for lower-latency int8 kernels on short sequences. Could that be causing alloc fragmentation/oversubscribe? :thinking:

sanjay: Perf trace (trimmed):
```
kernel_fallback_count: 153
kv_evictions: 308
avg_batch_size: 42
p50_latency: 0.22s
p99_latency: 1.20s
worker_restart_reasons: ["OOM","alloc_slab_failure"]
```
We see a lot of fallback to full-fp kernels and frequent KV cache churn; short requests are getting batched into large groups (40-60) which fills prefixes in KV.

eva: nvml/allocator snapshot shows high fragmentation: largest_contiguous_free < 200MB on affected GPUs. GC logs show repeated small frees and reallocs ~100-500KB which prevents large contiguous allocations. Looks like int8 kernels fragment allocator more in this workload.

ryan: Can we force the kernel selector back to legacy for that pool and reduce batching cap? I'll flip flag kernel.v2.enabled=false for pool=small-gpu-pool-3 and set batch_cap=16.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: feature flag kernel.v2.enabled=false rolled to small-gpu-pool-3 (3 nodes) at 12:58 UTC

kate: Also applied a hotpatch to batching heuristic: max_contiguous_batch_for_short=16 (rolling). That should prevent short prompts from coalescing into giant batches that inflate KV pressure.

sanjay: After the changes throughput recovered to ~98% of baseline within 6m. p99 fell from 1.20s -> ~430ms. No further OOMs or worker restarts in the last 12m.

ryan: Follow-ups: 1) Add per-tenant KV TTL for prefixes so tiny completions don't pin cache. 2) Add allocator defrag trigger (low-util mem compaction) between 03:00-04:00 UTC. 3) Capture detailed kernel-selection logs for any future kernel.v2 rollouts. I'll open tickets.

kate: Agreed. We should also add a canary step that runs a fragmentation microbenchmark before enabling v2 on small pools.

sanjay: Incident ticket created: https://redwood/issue/INF-3209 — include perf samples, kernel-selection traces, and nvml allocator stats. Thanks all.
